cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text:
Cost of sales includes raw material inputs, direct and indirect costs associated with the manufacturing and distribution of TRUTAKNA, amortization of capitalized intellectual property intangible assets and royalties payable on net sales of TRUTAKNA. Costs associated with the manufacture of TRUTAKNA prior to July 7, 2026, when we received accelerated approval from the FDA, were recorded as research and development expense. Recorded cost of sales will not represent the complete historical cost of inventory sold until we deplete stocks of inventory for which manufacturing or purchases of materials occurred prior to this date.

For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded cost of sales of $3.3 million related to sales of TRUTAKNA in the United States, compared to zero for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

opex.text: Research and development expenses represent a substantial portion of our operating expenses. Our research and development expenses consist primarily of direct and indirect expenses incurred in connection with the research and development of our lead product and product candidates. Direct expenses include costs incurred under agreements with third parties, including contract research organizations, contract drug manufacturing organizations and consultants directly related to our research and development of our lead product and product candidates, and license and milestone fees incurred as a result of our contractual obligations for our development candidates. Until we receive marketing approval for a product candidate, all drug manufacturing costs are expensed as research and development. Indirect expenses include employee compensation and other personnel-related expenses, including stock-based compensation, facilities and depreciation related to buildings and equipment used by research and development personnel and activities and other expenses.

rd.heading: Research and Development Expenses

Our research and development expenses consist primarily of direct and indirect expenses incurred in connection with the research and development of our lead product and product candidates. Direct expenses include costs incurred under agreements with third parties, including contract research organizations, contract drug manufacturing organizations and consultants directly related to our research and development of our lead product and product candidates, and license and milestone fees incurred as a result of our contractual obligations for our development candidates. Research and development expenses are recorded as expense in the period in which the related activities occurred, and payments we make prior to the receipt of goods or services to be used in research and development efforts are deferred as prepaid expenses until the goods or services are received and used.

Selling, general and administrative expenses also include professional fees paid for accounting, auditing, legal, tax and consulting services, and other general overhead costs to support our operations. Selling, general and administrative expenses are recorded as expense in the period in which they are incurred, and payments we make prior to the receipt of goods or services to be used for selling, general and administrative purposes are deferred as prepaid expenses until the goods or services are received and used.

nonop.text:
Other income, net, decreased by $1.6 million, or 45%, to $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $3.6 million in the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a decrease of $1.4 million in interest income resulting from lower average balances of marketable securities held during the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, and a decrease in sublease income of $0.5 million due to the expiration of a sublease to a third-party in September 2025, partially offset by a decrease of $0.1 million in amortization of deferred debt issuance costs for unfunded loan commitments relating to the refinancing of the Oxford credit facility in June 2025.

Other income, net, decreased by $3.6 million, or 29%, to $9.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $12.7 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a decrease of $2.9 million in interest income resulting from lower average balances of marketable securities held during the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 and a decrease in sublease income of $1.4 million due to the expiration of a sublease to a third-party in September 2025, partially offset by a $0.3 million change in realized and unrealized gains and losses, an increase of $0.2 million in cu.

net.text: We anticipate that we will continue to incur net losses for the foreseeable future as we continue research and development activities for our lead product and product candidates, hire additional staff, including clinical, commercial, operational, administrative and management personnel, and incur additional expenses associated with operating as a public company. We expect to incur significant expenses and operating losses for the foreseeable future as we continue to commercialize TRUTAKNA and advance our clinical development activities and our product candidate portfolio. We expect that our research and development and selling, general and administrative costs will increase substantially in connection with conducting additional clinical trials for our research programs, lead product, and product candidates, contracting with third parties to support nonclinical studies and clinical trials, expanding our intellectual property portfolio, scaling up external commercial manufacturing capacity, continuing to build a sales, marketing and distribution infrastructure to successfully commercialize TRUTAKNA and any other approved product candidates, and providing general and administrative support for our operations.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we used $305.9 million of cash in operating activities, attributable to a net loss of $324.2 million and an increase in our net operating assets and liabilities of $41.9 million, partially offset by $15.0 million in license fees attributable to investing activities and adjustments for non-cash charges of $45.2 million. Non-cash charges primarily consisted of $44.8 million of stock-based compensation and $1.9 million net in accretion and amortization of loan exit fees and costs, partially offset by non-cash interest income of $3.0 million related to amortization of discount on purchases of marketable securities. The change in our net operating assets and liabilities was primarily due to an increase of $24.4 million in prepaid expense and other current assets, an increase of $12.0 million in net accounts receivable, an increase of $7.1 million in inventory and a decrease of $1.7 million in accounts payable, partially offset by an increase of $3.6 million in accrued and other current liabilities.

net sales.heading: Product Revenue, Net
net sales.text:
To date, we have generated limited revenue from product sales. TRUTAKNA, our first approved product, received accelerated approval from the FDA in July 2026 to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary IgAN who are at risk for disease progression. We began selling TRUTAKNA in the United States in July 2026 through specialty pharmacy and specialty distributor customers.

Our net revenue from product sales depends on our prescription mix of commercial payors and governmental programs. Our revenue from product sales is recognized when the control of the product is transferred. In addition, we recognize our best estimate of the consideration that we expect to receive when control of the inventory is transferred to our customers, including reserves and accruals for discounts, distribution fees, product returns, chargebacks, rebates, co-pay assistance and other incentives. Such estimates may be complex and are reviewed and updated quarterly as additional information becomes known.

For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded net product revenue of $10.3 million from sales of TRUTAKNA.

intro.text: Vera Therapeutics is a commercial-stage biotechnology company focused on the pursuit of truth in science to transform medicine in autoimmune disease, starting with the kidney. Vera Therapeutics’ flagship commercial product is TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj), a BAFF and APRIL inhibitor indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary IgA nephropathy at risk for disease progression. Beyond IgAN, Vera Therapeutics is evaluating additional diseases where the reduction of autoantibodies through inhibition of BAFF and APRIL may prove clinically meaningful. Vera Therapeutics was founded in 2016 and is based in Brisbane, California. To learn more, visit www.veratx.com .

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.
